ref_kinds.published_table: a property table published outside this project
ref_kinds.published_closed_form: a closed form published outside this project, evaluated here
ref_kinds.independent_method: the same equations solved by a different method written for this artifact
ref_kinds.closed_form: a closed form of the tool’s own relation, evaluated independently

provenance_note: Recomputed in the page for every case whose reference is an independent route through the same equations (power iteration against the closed-form two-group eigenvalue, the linear reactivity model closed form, the geometric discount series, the interpolation node and monotonicity properties); recorded for the three case families whose reference is external — the published separative-work example, the IAPWS-IF97 densities and the explicit TRISO lattice runs measured while the library was built.
references: World Nuclear Association, "Uranium Enrichment": one kilogram of 5 % enriched uranium takes 7.9 SWU at 0.25 % tails and 8.9 SWU at 0.20 % tails.
M. J. Driscoll, T. J. Downar, E. E. Pilat, "The Linear Reactivity Model for Nuclear Fuel Management", ANS (1990): n-batch discharge burnup 2n/(n+1) times the single-batch value.
IAPWS-IF97, evaluated with the iapws 1.5.5 Python package, for the water density tables.
F. N. Fritsch, R. E. Carlson, "Monotone Piecewise Cubic Interpolation", SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 17 (1980) 238-246.
not_benchmarked: The lattice library itself: no independent integral benchmark of the OpenMC k-infinity values is published here, which is why the tool stands at prototype.
The interpolation of the library in enrichment between computed cases.
The operating-state model that maps power level to temperatures and void fraction.
The fuel-cycle prices, which are inputs rather than results.
